blocks.section: Wash Pump
blocks.content: This test will check the wiring to the wash/rinse motor and the motor itself. The following items are part of the wash/rinse motor circuit.

blocks.section: Test Procedure
blocks.content: Test Procedure

blocks.section: Test Procedure
blocks.content: Check the tub and sump for anything that may be impeding water flow. Inspect and if necessary clean the coarse-filter system. Also, inspect spray arm water nozzles and clean if needed.

blocks.section: Test Procedure
blocks.content: Check the wash pump and electrical connections by performing the 'Service Mode Test' on page 2-3. The following steps assume that this step was unsuccessful.

blocks.section: Test Procedure
blocks.content: Unplug dishwasher or disconnect power.

blocks.section: Test Procedure
blocks.content: Remove access panel. Remove control board cover to access control board.

blocks.section: Test Procedure
blocks.content: Lay the dishwasher on its back. Use a small flat-blade screwdriver to unclip snaps around the drip-pan. Remove drip-pan/float switch to access under tub components.

blocks.section: Test Procedure
blocks.content: Unplug connector CON1 and CON2 from control board.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: Figure 2 - Wash Pump Strip Circuit

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: Check the wash pump-using an ohmmeter, measure the resistance across the high and low pump coils as shown in the following chart.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: ¾ ¾ If the resistance is within range, the wash pump and harness are good. Go to step 8.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: ¾ ¾ If far outside the range, replace the wash pump.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: ¾ ¾ If an open circuit is detected, check connections and harness continuity between control and wash pump. If good, replace the wash pump.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: Reconnect CON1 and CON2 to control board.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: Test Wash Pump High Coil-Set voltmeter to AC and connect leads to CON2, pin 2 and CON1, pin 1 on the control board. Plug in dishwasher or reconnect power.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: Start the Service Mode Test and at the proper step measure for AC out of the control between CON2-2 and CON1-1. (Refer to Wash Motor Strip Circuit below.)

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: ¾ ¾ If no AC voltage is measured, replace the control board and retest.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: ¾ ¾ If 120 VAC is measured and wash pump is not running, go to step 12.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: ¾ ¾ If 120 VAC is measured and wash pump is running, go to step 14.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: Unplug dishwasher or disconnect power.  Repeat steps 9 and 10 for the Wash Pump Low Coil. Use pinouts CON2-3 and CON1-1.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: Test the wash pump capacitor. NOTE: A faulty capacitor may cause the motor to 'hum,' not start, or start slowly.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: Discharge the capacitor by touching the leads of a 20,000 Ω resistor to the two terminals.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: Disconnect the wires from the capacitor terminals.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: With an ohmmeter, measure across the terminals and note reading.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: ¾ ¾ If a steady increase in resistance is noted, capacitor is good. Replace wash motor assembly and retest.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: ¾ ¾ If the capacitor is either shorted or open, replace capacitor. and retest.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: If the preceding steps did not correct the wash/rinse motor problem, replace the control board.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: Unplug dishwasher or disconnect power.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: Reassemble all parts and panels.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.content: Plug in dishwasher or reconnect power and run 'Service Mode Test' to verify repair.

blocks.section: STRIP CIRCUIT - WASH PUMP WASH PUMP
blocks.markdown:
| MOTOR COIL   | PINOUTS                    | RESISTANCE   |
|--------------|----------------------------|--------------|
| High Coil    | CON2, Pin 2 to CON1, pin 1 | 44-54 ohms   |
| Low Coil     | CON2, Pin 3 to CON1, pin 1 | 69-87 ohms   |
